title: C Interview Craft & Classic Gotchas
relevance: Interviewers use classic C gotchas to probe memory safety, undefined-behavior awareness, and whether candidates recognize how language rules interact at the edges.

phases.goal: Establish the defensive C-interview posture and the core distinctions interviewers expect on sight.

must_hit.point: A C interview judges how you write code—NULL checks, leaks, and byte-level understanding—not only whether an algorithm is correct.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts algorithmic interviews with software focus on memory safety/UB/API design and hardware focus on interrupt-safety, bitwise fluency, and volatile/hardware boundaries.

must_hit.point: *p++ (same as *(p++)) yields the current pointed-to value then advances the pointer; (*p)++ increments the value at that location.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States that post-increment binds tighter than dereference, so *p++ does not increment the pointee.

must_hit.point: int *p[10] is an array of 10 pointers to int; int (*p)[10] is a pointer to an array of 10 ints.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Invokes the spiral rule or []-over-* precedence and notes parentheses force * to bind first.

must_hit.point: A dangling pointer refers to freed or out-of-scope memory (using it is UB); a leak is allocated memory never freed after its pointers are lost.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates stale/invalid address use from unreclaimable live allocations until process death.

must_hit.point: char *s = "hello" points at a read-only literal (typically .rodata); char s[] = "hello" copies into a mutable array.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says modifying via the pointer form can segfault; the array form is safe to change.

must_hit.point: static inside a function extends lifetime for the program while keeping local scope; at file scope it gives internal linkage to the translation unit.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names both lifetime and linkage meanings without conflating them with scope alone.

must_hit.point: Three common UB examples: dereferencing NULL/uninitialized pointers, out-of-bounds array access, and signed integer overflow.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those three and does not reduce UB to "it crashes" or "it wraps."

probes: What is the difference between *p++, (*p)++, and *(p++)?
What is the difference between a dangling pointer and a memory leak?
What are the two distinct meanings of the static keyword?

hints.1: Start from operator precedence and what free/return do to addresses.
hints.2: Separate pointer vs pointee mutation; separate invalid pointers from unreclaimed allocations; separate lifetime from linkage.
hints.3: *p++ advances p after yielding *p; (*p)++ bumps the int; dangling means freed/out-of-scope; static-in-function = program lifetime, file-static = internal linkage.

phases.goal: Show how declarations, macros, bits, layout, and qualifiers actually evaluate under the abstract machine.

must_hit.point: For char s[10] = "hi"; strlen(s) is 2 (chars before '\0'); sizeof(s) is 10 (compile-time allocated array size).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives both figures and warns that sizeof on a decayed parameter is the pointer size, not the array length.

must_hit.point: #define SQUARE(x) x * x makes SQUARE(1 + 2) expand to 1 + 2 * 1 + 2, evaluating to 5 not 9; arguments can also be evaluated twice (e.g. SQUARE(i++)).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows textual substitution ignoring precedence and prefers parenthesized macros or inline functions.

must_hit.point: A non-zero unsigned power of two satisfies (x & (x - 1)) == 0 because subtracting 1 clears the single set bit and lower bits.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains the one-bit-set property rather than looping with divide-by-2.

must_hit.point: Runtime endianness: set int num = 1, inspect the first byte via char*; *byte == 1 means little-endian.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Treats the int as a byte array and distinguishes byte-order from bit-order.

must_hit.point: sizeof(struct { char a; int b; }) may be 8 instead of 5 because the compiler inserts 3 padding bytes so int sits on a 4-byte-aligned address.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names padding for alignment and the serialization hazard of assuming packed layout.

must_hit.point: volatile forbids caching reads/writes in registers for values that may change outside the current thread—required for MMIO registers and ISR-shared globals.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States it stops compiler elision/caching and lists those two required cases.

must_hit.point: x |= 0x01 is load, OR, store; an ISR between load and store can be overwritten by the later store (read-modify-write hazard).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes the three assembly steps and that x++/bitwise ops are almost never atomic on a 32-bit MCU.

probes: How do strlen(s) and sizeof(s) differ for char s[10] = "hi";?
What is the pitfall of #define SQUARE(x) x * x?
What exactly does volatile do, and when is it required?
What is the read-modify-write atomicity hazard?

hints.1: Think compile-time size vs runtime length, then what the preprocessor literally pastes.
hints.2: Walk expansion of SQUARE(1+2); for volatile, say what the compiler may no longer assume; for RMW, expand |= into load/or/store.
hints.3: strlen→2, sizeof→10; SQUARE(1+2)→5; volatile for MMIO/ISR shared state; |= is three steps vulnerable to interrupt overwrite.

phases.goal: Choose constants, macros, and interview pacing deliberately instead of by habit.

must_hit.point: Prefer const for typed/unmodifiable values and parameters; #define for untyped textual substitution without scope; enum for related named integer constants with type and scope.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares the three and notes enum beats #define for state machines; flags C89 const-int array-size limits.

must_hit.point: Drive strategy: clarify constraints, ship a simple safe version first, only then refine with bitwise/pointer tricks, walk edges, and name UB that would make a shortcut invalid.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Orders clarify → brute force → optimize → edge cases → call out UB (e.g. signed overflow, strict aliasing).

must_hit.point: Macros are not function calls; inline functions are preferred for logic because macros ignore precedence and may evaluate arguments multiple times.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects "macros behave like calls" and cites parenthesization plus double-evaluation UB.

probes: When should you use const vs #define vs enum for constants?
How would you drive a C coding interview from first draft to a safe final answer?

hints.1: Ask what you need: type, scope, or preprocessor paste.
hints.2: Map const→typed/scoped, #define→text/no scope, enum→related ints; then describe baseline-before-cleverness.
hints.3: enum preferred for state machines over #define; write the safe version before bitwise tricks and explicitly reject UB shortcuts.

phases.goal: Apply the rules to interview traps, ISR constraints, and output-prediction puzzles.

must_hit.point: Returning a pointer to a local is always UB: stack storage dies on return and will be overwritten by later calls.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects "it sometimes works because it has not been overwritten yet."

must_hit.point: Do not call malloc or printf in an ISR: they are non-deterministic and lock-based; re-entering while the main loop holds the lock can deadlock.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties ISR needs (fast, deterministic) to lock re-entrancy and bans stdio/dynamic allocation in interrupt context.

must_hit.point: Array parameters decay to pointers, so sizeof(arr) in a function receiving char arr[] is the pointer size (usually 8 on 64-bit, 4 on 32-bit), not the original array size.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Traces "Antigravity" as 12 chars in main but sizeof in the callee as pointer width.

must_hit.point: Mixing unsigned int a = 10 with int b = -20 promotes -20 to unsigned, yielding a huge sum so a + b > 10 prints Greater.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Invokes usual arithmetic conversions and the unsigned reinterpretation of the negative operand.

must_hit.point: Writing a float via an unsigned int* violates strict aliasing (except char*); the compiler may ignore the write—use memcpy or a union (C99+) instead.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names strict aliasing, possible print of 1.000000, and the safe alternatives.

must_hit.point: i = i++ + 1 with no intervening sequence point between two modifications of i is undefined behavior—output is not predictable.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Identifies multiple modifications without a sequence point rather than guessing a printed value.

probes: Why is returning a pointer to a local variable disastrous?
Why can't you call malloc or printf inside an ISR?
What does the print_size("Antigravity") puzzle print, and why?
What does the unsigned/signed a + b > 10 puzzle print?

hints.1: Ask what happens to the stack frame, locks, and array parameters after the call boundary.
hints.2: Local addresses become dangling; ISR+printf can deadlock on re-entry; sizeof on a parameter is pointer-sized; signed/unsigned mixes promote.
hints.3: Always UB to return &local; no malloc/printf in ISR; sizeof→8 or 4; Greater after -20 becomes a huge unsigned.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Use const for typed unmodifiable values/parameters (still usually occupies memory); #define for untyped textual substitution with no scope; enum for related named integer constants with type and scope—better than #define for state machines. In older C (C89), a const int is not a constant expression for static array sizes, while #define or enum works.

tradeoffs.topic: Brute-force baseline vs immediate bitwise/pointer cleverness
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Clarify constraints (e.g. 32-bit int, whether string.h is allowed), write the simple safe version first, then optimize. Only after a working baseline move to bitwise or pointer-arithmetic solutions, walk empty/NULL/max-int edges, and reject shortcuts that rely on signed overflow or strict-aliasing violations.
Macros are textual and ignore call semantics: they can break precedence (SQUARE(1+2)→5) and evaluate arguments multiple times (SQUARE(i++) UB). Inline functions are preferred for logic.

tradeoffs.topic: volatile for MMIO/ISR shared state vs volatile for thread synchronization
tradeoffs.strong_answer: volatile is required so the compiler does not cache MMIO registers or ISR-updated globals, but it does not provide atomicity or stop CPU cache reordering—so it is the wrong tool to synchronize threads.

gotchas.correction: *p++ / *(p++) advances the pointer after yielding the current value; use (*p)++ to increment the pointee—otherwise you risk out-of-bounds reads.

gotchas.trap: Treating a pointer to an array as interchangeable with int **.
gotchas.correction: int (*p)[10] and int ** have different pointer-arithmetic scales; parentheses and [] vs * binding matter.

gotchas.trap: Thinking free(p) sets p to NULL.
gotchas.correction: free only returns memory to the allocator; p still holds the stale address and becomes dangling if used.

gotchas.trap: Thinking returning a pointer to a local "sometimes works" if not yet overwritten.
gotchas.correction: It is always undefined behavior; the stack object is destroyed on return.

gotchas.trap: Passing char *s = "hello" into a string-reversal routine that writes through s.
gotchas.correction: The literal is read-only (typically .rodata); modification can segfault—use a mutable char array copy instead.

gotchas.trap: Using sizeof on a decayed char s[] parameter expecting string or array length.
gotchas.correction: Inside the function it is a pointer; sizeof yields pointer size, not strlen or the original allocation.

gotchas.trap: Confusing static's scope with its lifetime, or forgetting file-scope linkage.
gotchas.correction: Function-static changes lifetime (program duration, local scope); file-static changes linkage to internal (translation-unit only).

gotchas.trap: Thinking macros behave like function calls.
gotchas.correction: They are textual: fix with ((x)*(x)) parenthesization, and prefer inline functions to avoid double evaluation and precedence bugs.

gotchas.trap: Detecting endianness by confusing bit-order with byte-order.
gotchas.correction: Endianness is about byte layout in memory; inspect bytes of an int (e.g. num = 1), not bit numbering myths.

gotchas.trap: Assuming structs pack with no padding when serializing to a socket or file.
gotchas.correction: Padding for alignment (e.g. 8 vs 5 for char+int) means direct struct dumps are layout-dependent and unsafe.

gotchas.trap: Believing UB just means "it crashes" or "it wraps around."
gotchas.correction: The compiler may assume UB never happens and optimize away checks, producing entirely unpredictable code.
volatile only blocks compiler caching/elision; it does not guarantee atomicity or prevent CPU cache reordering.

gotchas.trap: Assuming x++ or bitwise operators are atomic on a 32-bit MCU.
gotchas.correction: They almost never are; guard with temporarily disabled interrupts or true atomic instructions around the RMW.

gotchas.trap: Using standard-library I/O or dynamic allocation inside an ISR.
gotchas.correction: malloc/printf are non-deterministic and lock-based; re-entering from an ISR can deadlock if the main loop already holds the lock.
